Python: Primary language for backend systems, automation, AI/ML, and data engineering.
JavaScript: Essential for frontend interactivity, web development, and fullstack applications.
TypeScript: Adds static typing to JavaScript, highly favored for enterprise frontend and Node.js codebases.
Java: Standard enterprise backend language for robust, scalable microservices and high-throughput systems.
C++: High-performance systems programming language critical for game dev, finance, and embedded systems.
C#: Powers .NET enterprise platforms, enterprise web backends, and Unity game development.
Go: Lightweight, highly concurrent language popular for cloud infrastructure, microservices, and Kubernetes tooling.
Rust: Memory-safe systems programming language gaining rapid adoption in cloud infrastructure and performance-critical systems.
SQL: Fundamental query language for relational database management, data extraction, and reporting.
React: Industry-leading declarative UI library for building scalable single-page applications.
Vue.js: Progressive, lightweight JavaScript framework for clean and responsive user interfaces.
Angular: Comprehensive enterprise frontend framework with built-in dependency injection and TypeScript integration.
Next.js: Premier React framework for server-side rendering, static site generation, and modern web apps.
Node.js: Enables JavaScript execution on the server for asynchronous, event-driven web APIs.
Express.js: Minimalist web framework for Node.js commonly used to build RESTful APIs.
Django: High-level Python web framework with built-in ORM, authentication, and security features.
Flask: Lightweight and flexible Python micro-framework ideal for microservices and REST APIs.
FastAPI: Modern, high-performance Python framework for building APIs with automatic OpenAPI docs.
Spring Boot: Enterprise standard framework for building standalone production-grade Spring microservices.
Tailwind CSS: Utility-first CSS framework that accelerates modern UI and responsive design creation.
Bootstrap: Popular CSS framework for rapid prototype development and mobile-first layouts.
Docker: Containerization standard ensuring consistent application execution across development and production.
Kubernetes: Industry standard for automated container orchestration, scaling, and deployment management.
AWS: Dominant global cloud provider offering comprehensive compute, storage, and serverless solutions.
GCP: Google's cloud platform renowned for data analytics, Kubernetes (GKE), and machine learning capabilities.
Microsoft Azure: Enterprise cloud platform tightly integrated with Microsoft technologies and hybrid infrastructure.
Git: Universal version control system essential for collaborative code management and tracking.
GitHub: Primary platform for code hosting, continuous integration workflows (Actions), and open source collaboration.
CI/CD: Automation practice for continuous integration and continuous deployment that accelerates delivery pipelines.
Linux: Core operating system for server administration, cloud virtual machines, and container runtimes.
PostgreSQL: Advanced open-source relational database known for reliability, complex queries, and JSON support.
MySQL: Widely deployed relational database powering web applications and enterprise backends.
MongoDB: Leading document-oriented NoSQL database for flexible and unstructured data schemas.
Redis: In-memory data store used for ultra-fast caching, session storage, and message queues.
GraphQL: Query language for APIs that lets clients request exactly the data they need in a single roundtrip.
TensorFlow: End-to-end open-source machine learning platform developed by Google.
PyTorch: Leading deep learning framework favored in AI research and production computer vision / NLP.
Pandas: Essential Python data manipulation and analysis library for structured datasets.
Leadership: Key soft skill demonstrating initiative, mentoring capacity, and project ownership.
Communication: Crucial for conveying technical architecture and collaborating with cross-functional stakeholders.
Agile: Iterative project delivery methodology used across modern software development teams.
Scrum: Structured agile framework emphasizing sprint planning, daily standups, and retrospective delivery.
